blocks.raw: # Authentication
blocks.text: Authentication

blocks.raw: This page provides you with information on enabling basic auth and creating API client key and secret.
blocks.text: This page provides you with information on enabling basic auth and creating API client key and secret.

blocks.raw: Capillary supports three types of authentication:
blocks.text: Capillary supports three types of authentication:

blocks.raw:
1. Basic
2. OAuth
3. Authentication for end-customer web and mobile apps
blocks.text: BasicOAuthAuthentication for end-customer web and mobile apps

blocks.raw: # Basic authentication
blocks.text: Basic authentication

blocks.raw: In basic authentication, the till ID and password (in MD5 format) are used for authenticating the APIs. For information on creating a till ID and password, see [Add till](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/store-hierarchy-1#add-till).
blocks.text: In basic authentication, the till ID and password (in MD5 format) are used for authenticating the APIs. For information on creating a till ID and password, see Add till.

blocks.raw: By default, basic authentication is disabled for new organizations. To enable it, raise a ticket with the Product Support Team (PST).
blocks.text: By default, basic authentication is disabled for new organizations. To enable it, raise a ticket with the Product Support Team (PST).

blocks.raw: For existing organizations where basic authentication is already enabled and needs to be disabled, raise a ticket with the Product Support Team (PST).
blocks.text: For existing organizations where basic authentication is already enabled and needs to be disabled, raise a ticket with the Product Support Team (PST).

blocks.raw: # OAuth authentication
blocks.text: OAuth authentication

blocks.raw: OAuth (Open Authorization) is a standardized framework that enables secure and controlled access to resources, such as data and services, without requiring the sharing of sensitive credentials, like passwords.
blocks.text: OAuth (Open Authorization) is a standardized framework that enables secure and controlled access to resources, such as data and services, without requiring the sharing of sensitive credentials, like passwords.

blocks.raw: In OAuth, API client key and secret or access token are used for API authentication.
blocks.text: In OAuth, API client key and secret or access token are used for API authentication.

2. Navigate to the **Profile icon > Organization Settings > Tools > Authentication**.

6. In the **Description**, enter a short description of the client.

7. Select the **Allow access to sensitive information** checkbox if you want to allow the API client to access unmasked PSI data. If you leave this option disabled, API responses return PSI fields as masked when you use the OAuth token. This behaviour applies only <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/introduction-datamasking#enabling-data-masking">when organization-level PSI masking is enabled</Anchor>.

   <Image src="https://files.readme.io/6a0d8a2f1245d43a3baddeb32f1b7e884f07c3c1e038d955fcc8d54f1cbe0c22-image.png" align="center" width="35% " border={true} />

8. In **Token expiry duration**, set the default expiry for the tokens created for the client. By default, the maximum duration of an access token that you can set is configured as 60 minutes. An error message is displayed, if you try to set the token expiry duration for more than 60 minutes. This is for `/v3/oauth/token/generate`only. For information on creating an access token, see [Generating access token](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/oauth#generating-access-token).

8. In **Default till code**, enter default till code for the API and click **Validate**. If a till code is not passed in the API header, the default till is used for API attribution.
9. Select the default till code check box to use this till code for API attribution, If an invalid till is passed in the API header.
10. From the **Access group** drop-down, select the appropriate access group for your API client. For information on access groups, see [Access group](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/access-group). This access group restriction is applicable only for the API client and not the till.

blocks.raw: ## Creating an access token
blocks.text: Creating an access token

blocks.raw: You can use the API client key and secret and create an access token for authentication. For information on creating an access token, see [Generating access token](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/oauth#generating-access-token).
